newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends weak in pre-harvest hedging.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends weak in pre-harvest hedging.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled lower after a thinly traded session, and traders said the market was under pressure late from hedging tied to ideas that harvesting may begin this weekend in parts of Minnesota.

"Although there's a threat of some showers this weekend, we're drying out up here for the most part and there are thoughts that some harvesting may be under way this weekend in southern Minnesota," a MGE floor source said.
Traders said spring wheat was also under pressure on ideas that the current hot weather will reduce the risk of scab and other diseases that could negatively affect the crop.
MGE spring wheat closed 4-3/4 cents per bushel lower to 12 cents higher, with Sept down 4-3/4 cents at $3.85.
Traders said Prudential sold two million December bushels and Linnco sold around one million Dec. Country Hedging and Continental sold the Sept/Dec spread, traders said.
Friday's volume was estimated at 14.63 million bushels, down from Thursday's volume of 15.665 million bushels.
